content: The time to the first occurrence of one of the following events was assessed: hospitalization for angina pectoris, coronary revascularization, myocardial infarction, cardiovascular death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, hospitalization for heart failure, stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA), or peripheral vascular disease. The primary endpoint of the study is detailed below. The outcomes of this study were primarily influenced by the prevention of hospitalizations for angina and the reduction in the need for revascularization procedures. Effects observed in various subgroups are presented in the subsequent section. In an angiographic substudy conducted within the CAMELot trial (n=274), no significant difference was observed between amlodipine and placebo in terms of changes in atheroma volume within the coronary arteries, as assessed by intravascular ultrasound. The significant composite endpoint and clinical outcomes derived from the primary endpoint components are summarized below. Other components of the primary endpoint, including cardiovascular death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, myocardial infarction, hospitalization for heart failure, stroke/TIA, or peripheral vascular disease, did not show a statistically significant difference between amlodipine and placebo. Amlodipine was compared to placebo in four studies lasting 8–12 weeks, involving 697 patients with NYHA Class II/III heart failure. In these studies, there was no evidence of worsening heart failure based on measures such as exercise tolerance, NYHA classification, symptoms, or left ventricular ejection fraction. In an 8-month placebo-controlled mortality/morbidity study of amlodipine (5–10 mg) in 1,153 patients with NYHA Class III (n=931) or IV (n=222) heart failure on stable doses of diuretics, digoxin, and ACE inhibitors, amlodipine had no effect on the primary endpoint. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality and cardiac morbidity, defined as life-threatening arrhythmia, acute myocardial infarction, or hospitalization for worsening heart failure. There was also no effect on NYHA classification or heart failure symptoms. The total combined events of all-cause mortality and cardiac morbidity were 222/571 (39%) for patients on amlodipine and 246/583 (42%) for patients on placebo. Cardiac morbidity events accounted for approximately 25% of the endpoints in the study. Another study, PRAISE-2, randomized patients with NYHA Class III (80%) or IV (20%) heart failure without clinical symptoms or objective evidence of underlying ischemic disease, who were on stable doses of ACE inhibitors (99%), digitalis (99%), and diuretics (99%), to receive either placebo (n=827) or amlodipine (n=827). These patients were followed for a mean of 33 months. There was no statistically significant difference between amlodipine and placebo in the primary endpoint of all-cause mortality, with 95% confidence limits ranging from an 8% reduction to a 29% increase in mortality with amlodipine. However, there were more reports of pulmonary edema in the amlodipine group. Amlodipine is supplied as follows: NORVASC 5 mg tablets (amlodipine besylate equivalent to 5 mg of amlodipine per tablet) are white, elongated octagon-shaped, flat-faced, beveled-edged, engraved with NORVASC and 5 on one side and plain on the other. Bottle of 90 (NDC 0069-1520-68) Bottle of 300 (NDC 0069-1530-72) Unit dose package of 100 (NDC 0069-1530-41) NORVASC 10 mg tablets (amlodipine besylate equivalent to 10 mg of amlodipine per tablet) are white, round, flat-faced, beveled-edged, engraved with NORVASC and 10 on one side and plain on the other. Bottle of 90 (NDC 0069-1540-68) Unit dose package of 100 (NDC 0069-1540-41) Storage instructions: Store bottles at controlled room temperature, 59°F to 86°F (15°C to 30°C), and dispense in tight, light-resistant containers as per USP standards. Regarding alcohol interactions, single and multiple 10 mg doses of amlodipine did not significantly affect the pharmacokinetics of ethanol.
